text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: p99 latency breach on /v1/stream (shared-gpu-a) — p95 360ms, p99 1.9s over the last 5m. Error rate steady. Detected streaming stalls (clients seeing stalls ~2-4s). Affected customers: Acadia (tenant-id: t-acadia). Please ack and triage.

eric: acked. I'm on it. Starting collection for the pool.
maria: I'm joining. tagging infra: @dinesh for host IO checks. lia, can you loop in support for an immediate customer message? we should be transparent about degraded streaming.

dinesh: looking at node metrics for shared-gpu-a nodes. Disk IO for /dev/nvme0n1 on node shared-gpu-a-03 is very high (avg ~18k iops, 95th blkio latency 30ms). nvme saturation + high cgroup blkio wait could explain tail latency.

ben: running live queries against serving runtime. I see a spike in KV cache miss ratio and some backpressure in the streaming worker queue on instance ids [srv-118,srv-119]. Worker stalls correlate with blkio wait spikes.

maria: useful. can someone run a ps/ctr check to see which tenant is doing heavy IO? maybe a batch job leaked into shared pool.
eric: running container process list on shared-gpu-a-03. Found a long-running data-prep job under tenant t-veridian (process 8241) doing heavy reads to /mnt/datasets.

ben: that tenant shouldn't be on shared pool for large dataset reads. Do we have cgroup limits for blkio weight set? dinesh?
dinesh: blkio.weight was default (500). For that container it's 1000 due to older config. I'll post exact commands/outputs.

--- log snippet ---
```
# on shared-gpu-a-03
$ ls -l /proc/8241/cgroup
blkio:blkio:/docker/8241
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/8241/blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes
... (high read bytes from nvme) ...
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/8241/blkio.weight
1000
```
-------------------

lia: support-bot drafted a brief customer note for Acadia. Lia pasting: "We're investigating intermittent stalls on streaming. We're actively mitigating and will share updates in 30m. If you see production impacts please reply and we'll prioritize." Approve?
eric: approve. post now. lia please include guidance for retries/backoff in the interim.

support-bot: Message sent to Acadia workspace and created ticket INC-5921. Customer acknowledged: "We're seeing stalled chunks in our integration. Thanks for the heads up."

ben: mitigation plan proposal:
1) Throttle the noisy tenant by lowering their blkio.weight to 100.
2) Move long-running batch jobs to dedicated batch pool (if move fails, kill safest job candidate).
3) Temporarily increase serving capacity for shared-gpu-a (scale out 2 nodes) to reduce queuing.
4) Add short-term cgroup IO throttling rules for streaming-critical containers.

maria: +1. eric, can you change blkio.weight and scale? dinesh, can you help with safe eviction policy for batch jobs?
eric: applying step 1 now.

--- command ---
```
echo 100 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/8241/blkio.weight
kubectl scale deployment shared-gpu-a-nodes --replicas=7 -n runtime
```
---

eric: changed weight to 100. immediate drop in read bytes from that container confirmed. queue depth on srv-118 dropping.

dinesh: initiated batch job relocation. Kicking off move for job job-487 (non-critical nightly preprocess). If move completes, we'll keep it off shared pool. If move hangs, we'll terminate and restart on batch-dedicated.

ben: after weight change p95 improved to ~140ms and p99 now 520ms. Streaming stalls reduced. Still seeing occasional ~1s tail due to KV misses warming up.

maria: great. let's keep scaling until p99 < 500ms for 5m. ben, can you watch for regressions and post Prom queries you used?

ben: Prom queries:
```
# p95/p99 for /v1/stream latency
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/stream"}[5m])) by (le))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/stream"}[5m])) by (le))

# worker queue depth
sum(queue_depth{service="streaming"})
```

lia: customer message updated: "We've applied a mitigation and expect improvement. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary within 24h." Sent.

support-bot: Acadia replied: "Seeing much better now. Thanks team." Marking ticket as informed.

eric: runtime scale complete. monitoring for 10m.
dinesh: I'll add a short-term admission control to prevent batch scheduling onto shared-gpu pools until next deploy (patching scheduler config now).

maria: we should schedule a follow-up to tighten blkio defaults and enforce tenant placement checks at admission time. Also add an alert to detect long sequential NVMe reads from non-streaming tenants.

ben: agree. I'll open a follow-up RFC for cgroup/placement hardening and add a Prom rule for sustained read throughput per container.

maria: handoff to next on-call @eric (on shift for 30 more minutes) and then @maria will be primary for postmortem and remedial changes. Logging action items.

--- ACTIONS ---
- throttled tenant t-veridian blkio.weight -> 100 (eric)
- moved job-487 off shared pool (dinesh)
- scaled shared-gpu-a nodes +2 (eric)
- customer notified and acknowledged (lia/support-bot)
- create follow-up RFC & Prom rules (ben)
- schedule postmortem in 24h (maria)

maria: closing this triage thread. If p99 climbs again reopen. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident auto-note: severity=sev3, duration=~18m, impacted=Acadia (t-acadia).
